source.title_on_document: The Roles of Idea Generation and Elaboration in Human-AI Collaborative Creativity

supplement.where: Appendices A to D at the end of this PDF (pp. 32-34). Data on OSF: https://osf.io/nz6ag/?view_only=81c63168f1f64f62b2e865265b8ab343 (p. 8).
supplement.holds: Screenshots of the AI-help and No-AI interfaces (App. A, B), the prompt classification scheme (App. C), and prompt-count correlations without outlier removal (App. D). All condition contrasts are in the main text. No separate online supplement is referenced.

paper_design_summary: Penn State introductory psychology students (263 analyzed) each wrote two short stories of at least 150 words in an online study, one with free access to a GPT-3.5 chatbot (constrained to bullet-point ideas, copy-paste disabled) and one without AI; the order of the two conditions was randomized and the two three-word prompts were counterbalanced. Stories were scored for originality by an automated model (MAoSS) and for each story's contribution to semantic diversity of its prompt set (MiniLM sentence embeddings); participants also self-rated originality.

studies.label: Within-subjects story writing with and without ChatGPT

assignment.what_was_assigned: Order of the AI-help and No-AI story conditions (each participant wrote one story in each); the two three-word prompts (pen-paper-write, year-week-embark) were counterbalanced across conditions.
assignment.quote: Participants completed two stories, with (AI-help) and without AI help (No-AI). The order of presentation was randomized, such that an equal number of participants completed the AI-help and No-AI conditions first.

arms.name: AI-help
arms.description: Story written while chatting with ChatGPT (GPT-3.5 via custom API) in a side textbox; system prompt restricted output to bullet points and no full passages; copy-paste disabled; told to use ChatGPT as a 'source of ideas'.

arms.name: No-AI
arms.description: Same interface with the ChatGPT textbox removed; participants told to apply the practice prompting strategies to themselves as brainstorming.

participants.exclusions: 391 students recruited; 68 removed for reporting use of external aid (AI or internet) outside the provided AI; 53 removed for failing either of two attention checks; 7 removed for scoring below 2.5 SD on any intelligence test; final sample 263. The paper does not say whether exclusions came before or after order assignment, and gives no count at assignment. Each of the 263 contributes to both arms (within-subjects). Prompt-count analyses drop a further 2 (generation) and 7 (elaboration) outlier data points.
participants.who: Students enrolled in an introductory psychology course at Pennsylvania State University; 235 female, 27 male, 3 other (sums to 265, not 263); mean age 18.9 (SD 2.17); 95 percent had used ChatGPT or another LLM chatbot before.
participants.quote: In total, our final sample consisted of 263 participants (235 female, 27 male, 3 other; mean age = 18.9 years, SD = 2.17).

ai_tool.name_model: ChatGPT, GPT-3.5 base model via custom API
ai_tool.how_used: Participants freely sent messages to the chatbot in one textbox and wrote their story in another. A hidden system prompt framed the model as a creativity support tool and limited output to bullet points with no full story passages; copy-paste was disabled site-wide; participants were told not to ask it to write the story. All participants first did a practice story (50 words, ~2 minutes) with the same AI interface before either condition.

task.description: Adapted five-sentence short-story task: write a story of at least 150 words using all three words of a prompt (pen-paper-write or year-week-embark); instructed to 'use their imagination and be creative'.
task.duration: At least 10 minutes per story recommended but not enforced; submission blocked until 150 words.

outcomes.name: Story originality (MAoSS score)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Multilingual Assessment of Short Stories (MAoSS) model on the Creativity Assessment Platform: a fine-tuned LLM trained to predict human-rated originality; predictions correlate with human ratings at r = .86 (p. 11). Scale 0-1. Robustness: partial correlations controlling for word-count difference are reported only for the moderator analyses, not for the main condition contrast.

contrasts.reported: Paired-samples t-test: AI-help M = .56, SD = 08 [sic] vs No-AI M = .52, SD = 08 [sic]; t(262) = 5.56, p < .001, d = .34, 95% CI [.021, .045] (N = 263)
contrasts.locator: p. 14, Results, Story Originality; Figure 2 (left panel), p. 15

outcomes.name: Diversity contribution of each story
outcomes.question: across_people
outcomes.measure_detail: Dataset diversity = mean semantic distance (1 - cosine) over all pairs of stories in a prompt dataset, after removing the three prompt words. A story's diversity contribution = full-dataset diversity minus diversity with that story removed (leave-one-out); positive means the story adds diversity. Figure 2 plots values multiplied by 10^3.

contrasts.reported: Paired-samples t-test: AI-help M = -.000026, SD = .00033 vs No-AI M = .000027, SD = .00034; t(262) = -1.99, p = .047, d = -.123, 95% CI [-0.0001, -0.0000006] (N = 263). Lower = less diverse (more homogeneous).
contrasts.locator: p. 17, Results, Story Diversity; Figure 2 (middle panel), p. 15

diversity_detail.metric: Leave-one-out diversity contribution: mean pairwise semantic distance (1 - cosine) of the prompt dataset minus the same with the story removed
diversity_detail.computed_over: All pairs of stories within each prompt dataset (pen-paper-write or year-week-embark). Datasets are split by prompt, not by condition, so each dataset pools AI-help and No-AI stories; prompt words removed first.
diversity_detail.uncertainty: Paired-samples t-test across participants on the story-level contribution scores (df = 262).
diversity_detail.notes: Because the reference set pools both conditions, the measure is each story's contribution to diversity of the mixed pool, not within-arm diversity. Diversity difference scores (AI-help minus No-AI) were uncorrelated with AI integration and prompt counts (p. 17).

outcomes.name: Self-assessed originality and self-assessment accuracy
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Participants rated each story's originality on a 1-5 Likert scale. Accuracy = Kendall tau with MAoSS scores per condition, a multilevel model interaction (condition x self-assessment), and an error score (self-rating minus min-max rescaled MAoSS score). Listed for completeness; self-report does not satisfy criterion 3.

contrasts.reported: Kendall tau AI-help = 0.161, p < .001, 95% CI [.078, .244]; No-AI tau = 0.195, p < .001, 95% CI [.112, .278]. Interaction condition x self-assessment on MAoSS: t(413) = -0.22, p = .83, b = -0.001 (no SE printed). Self-assessment error AI-help M = 2.43, SD = 1.15; No-AI M = 2.14, SD = 1.18 (no test reported).
contrasts.locator: pp. 17-18, Results, Self-Assessment Accuracy; Figure 2 (right panel), p. 15

company_involvement.description: None stated. The AI was ChatGPT (GPT-3.5) called through OpenAI's API; funding is NSF and Aarhus University sources (p. 1).

eligibility.reason: Within-subjects design with randomized order of AI-help and No-AI conditions (p. 9), which the codebook accepts; 263 students analyzed (pp. 8-9); originality scored by an automated model and diversity by sentence embeddings on the stories (pp. 11-12). The abstract's word 'naturalistic' refers to free chat with the AI, not to non-random assignment.

one_line_finding: With ChatGPT, students' stories scored more original (MAoSS .56 vs .52; t(262) = 5.56, d = .34) but contributed less to semantic diversity (t(262) = -1.99, p = .047, d = -.123) than their own no-AI stories (pp. 14, 17).
open_questions: All participants did a practice story with the AI interface before either condition, and half wrote their No-AI story after the AI-help story; the paper reports no order or carryover analysis, so the No-AI arm is not AI-naive.
Exclusions (128 of 391) include 68 who reported using external aid; the paper does not say how this was split by condition or order, nor whether the count of 391 is at assignment.
The diversity measure's reference pool mixes AI-help and No-AI stories within each prompt set, so it is not a within-arm diversity comparison.
Originality SDs print as '08' (missing decimal point) on p. 14; the 95% CI [.021, .045] appears to be for the raw mean difference.
Gender counts (235 + 27 + 3 = 265) do not sum to the final N of 263 (p. 9).
notes: PDF pages carry no printed page numbers; locators use PDF page order. Correlational analyses of AI-response integration and generation/elaboration prompt counts (pp. 14-17, Figure 3, Appendix D) are within the AI-help arm and are not randomized contrasts, so they are not listed as outcomes. Word count was used only as a control in those analyses; no condition contrast on word count is reported. Design class coded online_rct: online Qualtrics study run on a course participant pool, not a supervised session.
